final.metaTitle: Compliance Updates — Renew Your Updates Window | Caisson
final.metaDescription: A $1,499/yr subscription that stamps a coverage horizon onto your Compliance bundle license, extending the per-entitlement updates window the registry Worker enforces on every pull at the edge.
final.heroOneLiner: Compliance Updates is the $1,499/yr subscription that keeps your Compliance license pulling new package versions — cancel it and the code you own keeps running, just frozen at its last covered release.
final.definition: Compliance Updates is the annual subscription that keeps a Compliance bundle license current with new package versions. Each paid cycle stamps a coverage horizon that computeUpdatesWindows folds into the buyer's per-entitlement updates window; the registry Worker's resolveGate and windowFilterEntry enforce it at the edge, so a version published after the window lapses is fail-closed invisible. It renews reach, never rewrites the code you already own.

included.title: Every paid cycle stamps a coverage horizon
included.body: upsertSubscriptionGrants() writes a subscription-sourced grant keyed to the Paddle subscription id on each granting invoice, setting updates_expires_at = now() + one cadence for the compliance entitlement — the mechanism the code comments still call the Compliance-Updates re-grant mirror.

included.title: computeUpdatesWindows folds the most-favorable bound
included.body: computeUpdatesWindows() reads the account's active one_time grants (updates_expires_at, or granted_at + 12 months) and takes the MAX against any live subscription coverage horizon — an active Compliance Updates subscription extends the window past what the original one-time bundle purchase alone would cover.

included.title: resolveGate resolves the per-module window at the edge
included.body: The registry Worker's resolveGate() reads the signed license's updatesWindows claim, expands the caller's purchased ids against the index, and folds the MOST FAVORABLE window per module — owning a module both à la carte and via the subscription-covered bundle applies whichever bound is later.

included.title: windowFilterEntry enforces fail-closed on every pull
included.body: windowFilterEntry() keeps only versions with publishedAt at or before the resolved cutoff and recomputes latest to the newest survivor; a module with zero in-window versions returns null — indistinguishable from a module the caller never bought.

included.title: Cancelling doesn't touch code you already pulled
included.body: The window mechanism only gates future registry reads, not local files: cancelling stops new coverage-horizon stamps, so a framework-mapping release published after your window closes won't pull — but nothing revokes or breaks the version already sitting in node_modules.

artifact.label: windowFilterEntry — the per-module version cutoff a lapsed subscription trips
annotations: versions.filter keeps only publishedAt <= cutoff — releases newer than your window aren't truncated to a stale pointer, they're dropped from the response entirely.
newest recomputes latest to the newest IN-WINDOW survivor, falling back off entry.latest the moment the index's real newest release falls outside your cutoff.
Returns null when nothing survives the filter — the caller reads exactly like a module they never bought, the same fail-closed 404 (ADR-0076).

faq.question: Is Compliance Updates the same as the Compliance bundle?
faq.answer: No. The Compliance bundle ($1,049, one-time) is the code; Compliance Updates ($1,499/yr) is the subscription that keeps its control mappings and evidence packs current as regulations change, by extending your license's per-entitlement updates window so new package versions keep pulling from the private registry.

faq.question: What does the subscription actually do, mechanically?
faq.answer: Each paid cycle stamps a coverage horizon on your account's compliance entitlement grant; computeUpdatesWindows folds that horizon into the window the registry Worker enforces at the edge (resolveGate + windowFilterEntry) — so a version published while your subscription is active stays pullable, one published after it lapses does not.

faq.question: What happens if I cancel?
faq.answer: You keep everything you already pulled — cancelling only stops new coverage-horizon stamps going forward. The audit chain, WORM store, and every field-crypto or compliance-core version already installed keeps running unrevoked; only future framework-mapping releases stop reaching you.

faq.question: Does this make my organization SOC 2 or HIPAA compliant?
faq.answer: No — no module or subscription makes an organization compliant; that determination is your organization's and its auditor's to make. Compliance Updates keeps the technical control mappings and evidence-pack generation current as SOC 2, HIPAA, and EU AI Act frameworks revise. The administrative controls and the audit itself remain yours.

sells.note: Sold standalone only at $1,499/yr — a subscription, not a bundle member; no one-time purchase includes it. It layers onto an owned Compliance bundle license ($1,049, one-time) or à-la-carte compliance modules already purchased — without an active one_time grant to extend, the subscription's coverage horizon has nothing to stamp.
